analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the growing focus on catch-up vaccination post-Covid-19 pandemic and assess the capacity of immunization programs to monitor delayed doses of measles-containing vaccines.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed WHO/UNICEF Joint Reporting Form data from 194 countries between 2016 and 2022, focusing on the availability of systems to track delayed childhood vaccination and quantifying catch-up doses of the first dose of a measles-containing vaccine (MCV1).
analysis_en.methods: The researchers evaluated the completeness and consistency of reporting systems, the proportion of delayed doses, and vaccination coverage, considering both timely and delayed administration, and analyzed the data by WHO Region, World Bank income classification, and Gavi support eligibility.
analysis_en.main_results: Results showed substantial variability across regions and income groups in countries’ ability to capture delayed doses, with the Region of the Americas reporting a higher proportion (77.1%–82.9%) of countries with systems to record delayed doses annually. Among countries with available data, the median proportion of delayed MCV1 doses was 4.4%, indicating an approximate 4 percentage point increase in reported coverage if catch-up doses were included.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as highlighting the need to improve immunization information systems to better capture delayed doses and explore the potential for increasing vaccination coverage and population immunity through catch-up activities.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform efforts to enhance global surveillance and monitoring of childhood vaccination timeliness, particularly in regions and income groups where systems for tracking delayed doses are less developed.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on self-reported data from immunization programs, which may introduce bias or inconsistencies, and the evidence is considered moderate due to the abstract-only nature of the analysis.

title_zh: 不让任何人掉队:使用世卫组织/联合国儿童基金会免疫联合报告表中的数据对儿童 疫苗接种 及时性和追赶情况进行监测的全球分析
source_body_en: In the years following the Covid-19 pandemic, immunization programmes have increasingly focused on the capacity to conduct and monitor catch-up vaccination—for doses administered later than the recommended schedule. However, it is unclear whether information systems are able to monitor delayed vaccination. We analyzed WHO/UNICEF Joint Reporting Form data from 194 countries (2016–2022) to understand if systems for tracking delayed childhood vaccination are available and quantify catch-up doses of the first dose of a measles-containing vaccine (MCV1). For Latin American and Caribbean countries, we also explored data for the third dose of diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis vaccine (DTP3). We assessed the completeness and consistency of reporting, the proportion of delayed doses, and vaccination coverage considering both timely and delayed administration. Analyses were disaggregated by WHO Region, World Bank income classification, and Gavi support eligibility. Results show substantial variability across regions and income groups in countries’ ability to capture delayed doses. Between 2016 and 2022, the proportion of countries reporting a system to record delayed doses ranged from 55.5% to 64.4% annually, with the Region of the Americas (AMR) consistently reporting a higher proportion (77.1%–82.9%). Among countries with available data, the median proportion of delayed MCV1 doses was 4.4%, suggesting that including catch-up doses in cohort monitoring would increase reported coverage by approximately 4 percentage points. This increase was smaller in Gavi-eligible countries compared with non-eligible countries. The study summarizes global differences in information systems to monitor catch-up vaccination, presents examples of cohort coverage monitoring and illustrates the need to further improve immunization information systems and explore the potential for improving vaccination coverage and population immunity through catch-up activities.
abstract_zh: 在 Covid-19 大流行之后的几年中,免疫计划越来越关注执行和监测 疫苗接种 补种的能力(即晚于建议时间表施用的剂量)。然而,目前尚不清楚信息系统是否能够监控延迟的疫苗接种。我们分析了来自 194 个国家(2016-2022 年)的 WHO/UNICEF 联合报告表数据,以了解追踪延迟儿童 疫苗接种 的系统是否可用,并量化含 麻疹 的 疫苗 (MCV1) 第一剂的追赶剂量。对于拉丁美洲和加勒比国家,我们还探讨了第三剂白喉-破伤风-百日咳 疫苗 (DTP3) 的数据。我们评估了报告的完整性和一致性、延迟剂量的比例以及考虑及时和延迟给药的 疫苗接种 覆盖范围。分析按世卫组织区域、世界银行收入分类和全球疫苗和免疫联盟支持资格进行分类。结果显示,不同地区和收入群体的国家捕获延迟剂量的能力存在很大差异。2016 年至 2022 年间,每年报告有记录延迟剂量系统的国家比例为 55.5% 至 64.4%,其中美洲地区 (AMR) 报告的比例始终较高 (77.1%–82.9%)。在有可用数据的国家中,延迟 MCV1 剂量的中位数比例为 4.4%,这表明在 队列研究 监测中纳入追赶剂量将使报告的覆盖率增加约 4 个百分点。与不符合条件的国家相比,符合全球疫苗免疫联盟条件的国家的增幅较小。该研究总结了监测追赶疫苗接种的信息系统的全球差异,介绍了队列研究覆盖率监测的例子,并说明需要进一步完善免疫信息系统,并探索通过追赶活动提高疫苗接种覆盖率和人群免疫力的潜力。

title: A mark and recapture perspective on vaccination touchpoints
abstract: This paper considers large-scale vaccination campaigns, a major platform for vaccine access in a lot of the world, as a recapture estimate of the target population marked by routine immunization. Framing the campaign as a measurement, we learn about its properties, including the campaign’s coverage of the target population and some implied sampling properties of post-campaign coverage surveys (PCCSs), the current gold-standard in implementation quality measurement. We develop this idea in the context of the 2023 measles campaign in Kano State, Nigeria, where we have detailed implementation data collected by vaccination teams involved in that effort. Looking specifically at the teams’ tally sheets, the daily records of who they vaccinated, we find significant discrepancies between the recapture estimates and those from the corresponding PCCS. Exploring a variety of bias models applied to both the tally sheets and the PCCS helps clarify how anecdotal issues from the field relate to this discrepancy. Overall, we find that the tally sheets, despite being an unorthodox population sample, provide a tractable perspective on implementation and measurement, one that’s in principle available nearly instantly and at high resolution for any vaccination touchpoint.

analysis.summary_en: This paper explores the use of a mark and recapture framework to analyze vaccination campaigns, particularly focusing on measles virus-related efforts. It frames vaccination campaigns as a method to estimate population coverage and evaluates the properties of these campaigns, including their alignment with post-campaign coverage surveys (PCCSs). The study uses detailed implementation data from the 2023 measles campaign in Kano State, Nigeria, to demonstrate that tally sheets, despite being unconventional, can provide a high-resolution and immediate perspective on vaccination touchpoints. The paper identifies discrepancies between tally sheet data and PCCS results, and explores bias models to understand these differences. The findings suggest that tally sheets may serve as a valuable tool for assessing implementation quality, offering an alternative to traditional surveys.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本文将大规模疫苗接种活动,作为全球许多地区疫苗访问的主要平台,视为一种重新捕捉估计,以评估常规免疫接种所标记的目标人群。麻疹病毒(Morbillivirus hominis)的历史分类名称、麻疹(rubeola)和麻疹疾病是研究重点。核心问题是:如何利用标记与重新捕捉框架分析疫苗接种接触点,以评估实施质量。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 将活动作为一种衡量标准,我们了解其属性,包括活动对目标人群的覆盖范围以及活动后覆盖率调查(PCCS)的一些隐含抽样属性,这是当前实施质量衡量的黄金标准。审查方法涉及分析 疫苗接种 团队在尼日利亚卡诺州参与 2023 年 麻疹 活动所收集的实施数据。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 我们在尼日利亚卡诺州 2023 年 麻疹 活动的背景下提出了这一想法,我们拥有参与该活动的 麻疹 团队收集的详细实施数据。总的来说,我们发现,尽管统计表是一个非正统的人口样本,但它提供了一种易于处理的实施和测量视角,原则上几乎可以立即以高分辨率获取任何 疫苗接种 接触点。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 特别查看各队的统计表以及他们接种疫苗的每日记录,我们发现重新捕获估计值与相应 PCCS 的估计值之间存在显着差异。探索应用于统计表和 PCCS 的各种偏差模型有助于澄清现场的轶事问题与这种差异之间的关系。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 其含义表明,统计表可以提供一种高分辨率、近乎即时的方法来评估实施质量,这可以补充传统的活动后覆盖率调查。

title_zh: 从标记与重新捕捉视角审视疫苗接种接触点
source_body_en: This paper considers large-scale vaccination campaigns, a major platform for vaccine access in a lot of the world, as a recapture estimate of the target population marked by routine immunization. Framing the campaign as a measurement, we learn about its properties, including the campaign’s coverage of the target population and some implied sampling properties of post-campaign coverage surveys (PCCSs), the current gold-standard in implementation quality measurement. We develop this idea in the context of the 2023 measles campaign in Kano State, Nigeria, where we have detailed implementation data collected by vaccination teams involved in that effort. Looking specifically at the teams’ tally sheets, the daily records of who they vaccinated, we find significant discrepancies between the recapture estimates and those from the corresponding PCCS. Exploring a variety of bias models applied to both the tally sheets and the PCCS helps clarify how anecdotal issues from the field relate to this discrepancy. Overall, we find that the tally sheets, despite being an unorthodox population sample, provide a tractable perspective on implementation and measurement, one that’s in principle available nearly instantly and at high resolution for any vaccination touchpoint.
abstract_zh: 本文将大规模疫苗接种活动视为一种重新捕捉估计,作为常规免疫接种所标记目标人群的估计方法。将该活动视为一种测量手段,我们探讨其特性,包括该活动对目标人群的覆盖率以及活动后覆盖率调查(PCCS)的一些隐含抽样特性,后者是当前实施质量测量的黄金标准。我们以2023年尼日利亚卡诺州麻疹活动为背景,发展这一想法,该活动有疫苗接种团队详细收集的实施数据。具体分析这些团队的统计表,以及他们每日记录的接种对象,我们发现重新捕捉估计与相应PCCS的估计之间存在显著差异。探讨应用于统计表和PCCS的各种偏差模型有助于阐明现场轶事问题如何与这种差异相关联。总体而言,我们发现尽管统计表是一种非常规的人群样本,但它们为实施和测量提供了可行的视角,这种视角原则上可以几乎即时获得,并且对任何疫苗接种接触点都具有高分辨率。
summary_zh: 本文将大规模疫苗接种活动视为一种重新捕捉估计,作为常规免疫接种所标记目标人群的估计方法。将该活动视为一种测量手段,我们探讨其特性,包括该活动对目标人群的覆盖率以及活动后覆盖率调查(PCCS)的一些隐含抽样特性,后者是当前实施质量测量的黄金标准。我们以2023年尼日利亚卡诺州麻疹活动为背景,发展这一想法,该活动有疫苗接种团队详细收集的实施数据。具体分析这些团队的统计表,以及他们每日记录的接种对象,我们发现重新捕捉估计与相应PCCS的估计之间存在显著差异。探讨应用于统计表和PCCS的各种偏差模型有助于阐明现场轶事问题如何与这种差异相关联。总体而言,我们发现尽管统计表是一种非常规的人群样本,但它们为实施和测量提供了可行的视角,这种视角原则上可以几乎即时获得,并且对任何疫苗接种接触点都具有高分辨率。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本文将大规模疫苗接种活动,作为全球许多地区疫苗访问的主要平台,视为一种重新捕捉估计,以评估常规免疫接种所标记的目标人群。麻疹病毒(Morbillivirus hominis)的历史分类名称、麻疹(rubeola)和麻疹疾病是研究重点。核心问题是:如何利用标记与重新捕捉框架分析疫苗接种接触点,以评估实施质量。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 将活动作为一种衡量标准,我们了解其属性,包括活动对目标人群的覆盖范围以及活动后覆盖率调查(PCCS)的一些隐含抽样属性,这是当前实施质量衡量的黄金标准。审查方法涉及分析 疫苗接种 团队在尼日利亚卡诺州参与 2023 年 麻疹 活动所收集的实施数据。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 我们在尼日利亚卡诺州 2023 年 麻疹 活动的背景下提出了这一想法,我们拥有参与该活动的 麻疹 团队收集的详细实施数据。总的来说,我们发现,尽管统计表是一个非正统的人口样本,但它提供了一种易于处理的实施和测量视角,原则上几乎可以立即以高分辨率获取任何 疫苗接种 接触点。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 特别查看各队的统计表以及他们接种疫苗的每日记录,我们发现重新捕获估计值与相应 PCCS 的估计值之间存在显着差异。探索应用于统计表和 PCCS 的各种偏差模型有助于澄清现场的轶事问题与这种差异之间的关系。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 其含义表明,统计表可以提供一种高分辨率、近乎即时的方法来评估实施质量,这可以补充传统的活动后覆盖率调查。

title: Immunization dropout rate and associated factors among children aged 12-35 months in a rural field practice area: a community-based cross-sectional study
abstract: Background: Immunization is one of the most effective public health interventions for preventing vaccine-preventable diseases and reducing under-five morbidity and mortality. Despite improvements in vaccination coverage under the Universal Immunization Programme, some children fail to complete the recommended schedule. Immunization dropout reflects gaps related to caregivers, health services, and accessibility, making its assessment essential for improving complete immunization coverage. Methods: A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 400 children aged 12-35 months residing in the selected study area. Participants were selected using multistage random sampling. Data were collected using a pre-tested semi-structured questionnaire and verified using immunization cards wherever available. Dropout rates were calculated using WHO indicators, including BCG-to-Measles/MR and Pentavalent-1-to-Pentavalent-3 dropout rates. Associations were assessed using the Chi-square test, followed by multivariable logistic regression. A p value 5 km from a health facility were significant independent determinants. Conclusions: Strengthening caregiver awareness, defaulter tracking, card retention, institutional deliveries, and accessibility of vaccination services may reduce immunization dropout and improve complete immunization coverage.
journal: International Journal of Community Medicine and Public Health

title: Strengthening post-disaster disease surveillance through field epidemiology support in Indonesia, 2025
abstract: Problem: Natural disasters increase the risk of communicable disease transmission while disrupting routine disease surveillance systems, leading to delayed detection of outbreaks and weakened public health decision-making during emergency responses. Context: Indonesia is vulnerable to natural hazards, and Aceh Province has experienced recurrent disasters with significant public health impacts. In late 2025, major flooding and landslides affected Aceh Tamiang District, disrupting health services. Field epidemiology support was deployed to strengthen post-disaster disease surveillance during the emergency response. Action: A field epidemiologist strengthened case detection and registration at health posts, standardized disease recording, verified suspected clusters, and established centralized data compilation, analysis and situation reporting via the Health Emergency Operations Centre. Activities were aligned with World Health Organization functions and were adapted to emergency conditions. Outcome: There was substantial disruption to routine health services, with severe damage to 12 of 15 primary health-care centres and the district health office, and moderate damage to two hospitals. Nevertheless, core surveillance functions were maintained during the emergency response, facilitating the reporting and documentation of multiple outbreak-prone diseases, including typhoid, measles and varicella. Surveillance outputs were used to inform timely risk assessment and response actions, including mobilizing laboratory surge capacity to support diagnostic activities. Discussion: Concrete actions translate field data into timely, structured public health responses. Field epidemiologists can help maintain system functionality in resource-constrained emergencies by adapting to paper and mobile tools, synthesizing fragmented data and coordinating directly with laboratory personnel for case confirmation.

Nevertheless, core surveillance functions were maintained during the emergency response, facilitating the reporting and documentation of multiple outbreak-prone diseases, including typhoid, measles and varicella. Surveillance outputs were used to inform timely risk assessment and response actions, including mobilizing laboratory surge capacity to support diagnostic activities. Discussion: Concrete actions translate field data into timely, structured public health responses. Field epidemiologists can help maintain system functionality in resource-constrained emergencies by adapting to paper and mobile tools, synthesizing fragmented data and coordinating directly with laboratory personnel for case confirmation.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在解决自然灾害破坏常规系统并增加传染病传播风险的挑战。研究旨在评估现场流行病学支持在加强灾后疾病监测方面的有效性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究在印度尼西亚亚齐坦iang区进行,该地区在2025年底经历了严重的洪水和山体滑坡。研究涉及在现场部署流行病学支持以增强应急响应期间的疾病监测能力。

title: A Duty to Act
abstract: Throughout our history, the healthcare and scientific communities have united in the face of public health crises to save lives. During natural disasters like hurricanes or wildfires, infectious diseases outbreaks and pandemics, and longstanding threats like tobacco use, robust and unified responses from healthcare professionals and scientists have delivered information, innovation, and care that has empowered millions of Americans to lead longer, healthier, and more fulfilling lives [1,2]. Taken together, the current spread of misinformation by federal health agencies and the dismantling of much of our public health and medical research infrastructure and healthcare safety net constitute another crisis that has already claimed American lives and is poised to do even greater damage to our nation's health. Once again, healthcare professionals and scientists have a duty to act. Our patients and communities are counting on us. The impacts of the current administration's actions rise above typical partisan disagreements to pose a major threat to the health of the American people. Consider the following examples: Access to healthcare: The Congressional Budget Office estimates that about 10 million people will lose health insurance as a result of the so-called Big Beautiful Bill. That will result in more people getting delayed diagnoses and care, leading to poorer outcomes, higher costs, and more emergency department utilization [3]. Healthcare workforce: To further increase barriers to care, the administration is cutting clinician reimbursement, downgrading the essential profession of nursing to restrict access to student loan forgiveness programs, and limiting the ability of health professionals from other countries to work in the United States by tampering with our visa systems. All of these policies strike at the heart of our healthcare workforce, curtailing recruitment and retention of highly trained professionals who were already suffering workforce shortages and burnout [4–6]. Research: America's scientific research engine has long been a world leader, inspiring generations of researchers to deliver new tools to prevent, detect, and treat diseases, lengthening the human lifespan and improving our quality of life. Scientific breakthroughs take years and require predictability of funding. This administration introduced chaos into our grantmaking processes, arbitrarily freezing grants, proposing massive funding cuts, halting international scientific collaborations, and injecting politics into longstanding grant review processes. This will slow the pace of lifesaving scientific advances, discourage a generation from pursuing research careers in the United States, cause our nation to fall behind globally, and leave Americans less prepared to face the next health threat [7]. Public health: The exodus of experts from the Centers for Disease Control (CDC) and other Health and Human Services (HHS) agencies coupled with the loss of funding for state and local health departments leaves Americans profoundly less safe, less prepared for emergencies, and less capable of tackling public health problems like obesity, tobacco use, substance abuse, and outbreaks of infectious diseases. The administration's cuts will delay and limit our ability to identify and track new pathogens, which will allow more people to get sick and slow our ability to offer testing, prevention strategies, and optimal care [8]. Vaccines: The purposeful erosion of vaccine confidence, access, and uptake is already having devastating effects on our population, as evidenced by the explosion of measles cases in the United States. The administration's dismissal of CDC's independent expert vaccine advisors and replacement with politically influenced science deniers has created significant confusion and chaos among patients, families, and clinicians; restricted access to lifesaving vaccines and significantly damaged the credibility of what was once the premier public health agency in the world. While recent legal actions have stayed most of the new appointments and votes of the CDC Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices and the HHS changes to the pediatric immunization schedule, many legal issues are still pending, and it will take a significant and concerted effort to rebuild US vaccine infrastructure and help the public access and discern credible vaccine information. It is important to recognize that while the assault on science and health impact us all, the most vulnerable—low-income individuals, people of color, those living in rural communities, immigrants, lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer (LGBTQ) people, older adults, babies, and the immunocompromised and others with significant medical needs—are bearing the brunt of the consequences. As healthcare professionals and scientists, we have always taken care of those in greatest need, and the need has never been greater than it is right now. While it is easy to despair at the breadth and barrage of attacks on our health, we have an ethical obligation to our patients and communities to resist these changes. We must do more than simply aim to protect the status quo. Let ’s face it—deep dissatisfaction with the status quo is, in part, what led us to the current moment. We know that our longstanding systems were steeped in inequities and failing too many people. We must seize this opportunity to create something far better: a low barrier, person-centered healthcare system that serves everyone, a stronger public health infrastructure that meets the needs of all communities and innovative medical research that prioritizes patients. As healthcare professionals and scientists, our training and lived experiences provide us with a wealth of knowledge that we can use to stand up for science and improve our nation's health in a systemic way. In addition, our professional roles make us trusted voices in our communities. Banding together, we can elevate our voices further for the betterment of all. What can that look like? Educate: We have many opportunities to educate colleagues, family members, patients, and friends, by listening to their concerns and responding with factual information and without judgment. We can clearly explain how different policies are impacting us and those around us. Working with our professional societies, we can use traditional and nontraditional media to get our messages out to wider audiences. A better educated populace can more effectively sway their elected officials and make more informed decisions in future elections. Advocate: We can also urge our lawmakers to base policies on the best available scientific evidence and provide adequate funding for healthcare, public health, and medical research. Our professional societies provide an array of tools to support advocacy, including trainings, talking points, online mechanisms to contact Congress, advocacy days, and more. It is critical that Senators and Representatives hear from their constituents and face pressure from their states and districts to stand up to the administration and advance policies that align with their constituents’ best interests. Run: Fundamentally, if we want better policies, we need better policymakers. Who better than healthcare professionals and scientists to drive a policy agenda steeped in science and geared toward improving the health of all? The 314 Action PAC provides support to Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) professionals who run for office at the state or national level, recognizing that our voices are essential in the halls of Congress and our state legislatures. Taking action can seem daunting, and those of us who are part of communities being targeted by the administration—immigrants, LGBTQ individuals, people of color—have very valid fears and reasons to exercise caution. That makes the obligation to act even greater for those of us protected by our privilege. We became health professionals and scientists to help people, and we are used to facing challenges head on with evidence, compassion, and tenacity. Those are the very qualities our nation needs now.

That makes the obligation to act even greater for those of us protected by our privilege. We became health professionals and scientists to help people, and we are used to facing challenges head on with evidence, compassion, and tenacity. Those are the very qualities our nation needs now.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need for healthcare professionals and scientists to respond to the current crisis of misinformation and weakened public health infrastructure, which threatens the health of the American people. The authors highlight the importance of unified action in the face of public health challenges, as seen historically.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a policy analysis focusing on the United States, examining the impact of current administration policies on healthcare access, workforce, research, and public health infrastructure. It involves a broad population of healthcare professionals, scientists, and the general public affected by these policies.
analysis.methods: The methods involve reviewing the effects of specific policies on healthcare systems, analyzing the consequences of funding cuts and changes in public health infrastructure, and assessing the impact on vaccine confidence and access through legal and policy changes.
analysis.main_results: The study reports that the administration's policies have led to a projected loss of 10 million health insurance beneficiaries, increased barriers to care, and a decline in scientific research predictability. These actions have created confusion and chaos in public health, particularly regarding vaccine programs.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as evidence of a significant threat to public health and scientific progress, emphasizing the need for a more equitable and robust healthcare system. The novelty lies in highlighting the ethical duty of healthcare professionals and scientists to act against these policies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the urgent need for advocacy and education to protect public health infrastructure, ensure equitable access to healthcare, and maintain scientific integrity in policy-making, particularly concerning vaccine programs and research funding.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is based on policy analysis and legal actions, which may not provide direct empirical data. However, the implications are supported by the cited examples and the authors' ethical stance, leading to a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This policy analysis highlights the current crisis in the United States, driven by misinformation, weakened public health infrastructure, and harmful policies that threaten healthcare access, research, and vaccine programs. The authors argue that these actions have already claimed American lives and pose a major threat to public health. They emphasize the ethical duty of healthcare professionals and scientists to act, advocating for a more equitable healthcare system and robust public health infrastructure. The study underscores the need for education and advocacy to counteract these policies and protect the health of vulnerable populations. While the evidence is based on policy and legal changes, it provides a compelling case for the importance of science-based decision-making in public health.

During natural disasters like hurricanes or wildfires, infectious diseases outbreaks and pandemics, and longstanding threats like tobacco use, robust and unified responses from healthcare professionals and scientists have delivered information, innovation, and care that has empowered millions of Americans to lead longer, healthier, and more fulfilling lives [1,2]. Taken together, the current spread of misinformation by federal health agencies and the dismantling of much of our public health and medical research infrastructure and healthcare safety net constitute another crisis that has already claimed American lives and is poised to do even greater damage to our nation's health. Once again, healthcare professionals and scientists have a duty to act. Our patients and communities are counting on us. The impacts of the current administration's actions rise above typical partisan disagreements to pose a major threat to the health of the American people. Consider the following examples: Access to healthcare: The Congressional Budget Office estimates that about 10 million people will lose health insurance as a result of the so-called Big Beautiful Bill. That will result in more people getting delayed diagnoses and care, leading to poorer outcomes, higher costs, and more emergency department utilization [3]. Healthcare workforce: To further increase barriers to care, the administration is cutting clinician reimbursement, downgrading the essential profession of nursing to restrict access to student loan forgiveness programs, and limiting the ability of health professionals from other countries to work in the United States by tampering with our visa systems. All of these policies strike at the heart of our healthcare workforce, curtailing recruitment and retention of highly trained professionals who were already suffering workforce shortages and burnout [4–6]. Research: America's scientific research engine has long been a world leader, inspiring generations of researchers to deliver new tools to prevent, detect, and treat diseases, lengthening the human lifespan and improving our quality of life. Scientific breakthroughs take years and require predictability of funding. This administration introduced chaos into our grantmaking processes, arbitrarily freezing grants, proposing massive funding cuts, halting international scientific collaborations, and injecting politics into longstanding grant review processes. This will slow the pace of lifesaving scientific advances, discourage a generation from pursuing research careers in the United States, cause our nation to fall behind globally, and leave Americans less prepared to face the next health threat [7]. Public health: The exodus of experts from the Centers for Disease Control (CDC) and other Health and Human Services (HHS) agencies coupled with the loss of funding for state and local health departments leaves Americans profoundly less safe, less prepared for emergencies, and less capable of tackling public health problems like obesity, tobacco use, substance abuse, and outbreaks of infectious diseases. The administration's cuts will delay and limit our ability to identify and track new pathogens, which will allow more people to get sick and slow our ability to offer testing, prevention strategies, and optimal care [8]. Vaccines: The purposeful erosion of vaccine confidence, access, and uptake is already having devastating effects on our population, as evidenced by the explosion of measles cases in the United States. The administration's dismissal of CDC's independent expert vaccine advisors and replacement with politically influenced science deniers has created significant confusion and chaos among patients, families, and clinicians; restricted access to lifesaving vaccines and significantly damaged the credibility of what was once the premier public health agency in the world. While recent legal actions have stayed most of the new appointments and votes of the CDC Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices and the HHS changes to the pediatric immunization schedule, many legal issues are still pending, and it will take a significant and concerted effort to rebuild US vaccine infrastructure and help the public access and discern credible vaccine information. It is important to recognize that while the assault on science and health impact us all, the most vulnerable—low-income individuals, people of color, those living in rural communities, immigrants, lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer (LGBTQ) people, older adults, babies, and the immunocompromised and others with significant medical needs—are bearing the brunt of the consequences. As healthcare professionals and scientists, we have always taken care of those in greatest need, and the need has never been greater than it is right now. While it is easy to despair at the breadth and barrage of attacks on our health, we have an ethical obligation to our patients and communities to resist these changes. We must do more than simply aim to protect the status quo. Let ’s face it—deep dissatisfaction with the status quo is, in part, what led us to the current moment. We know that our longstanding systems were steeped in inequities and failing too many people. We must seize this opportunity to create something far better: a low barrier, person-centered healthcare system that serves everyone, a stronger public health infrastructure that meets the needs of all communities and innovative medical research that prioritizes patients. As healthcare professionals and scientists, our training and lived experiences provide us with a wealth of knowledge that we can use to stand up for science and improve our nation's health in a systemic way. In addition, our professional roles make us trusted voices in our communities. Banding together, we can elevate our voices further for the betterment of all. What can that look like? Educate: We have many opportunities to educate colleagues, family members, patients, and friends, by listening to their concerns and responding with factual information and without judgment. We can clearly explain how different policies are impacting us and those around us. Working with our professional societies, we can use traditional and nontraditional media to get our messages out to wider audiences. A better educated populace can more effectively sway their elected officials and make more informed decisions in future elections. Advocate: We can also urge our lawmakers to base policies on the best available scientific evidence and provide adequate funding for healthcare, public health, and medical research. Our professional societies provide an array of tools to support advocacy, including trainings, talking points, online mechanisms to contact Congress, advocacy days, and more. It is critical that Senators and Representatives hear from their constituents and face pressure from their states and districts to stand up to the administration and advance policies that align with their constituents’ best interests. Run: Fundamentally, if we want better policies, we need better policymakers. Who better than healthcare professionals and scientists to drive a policy agenda steeped in science and geared toward improving the health of all? The 314 Action PAC provides support to Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) professionals who run for office at the state or national level, recognizing that our voices are essential in the halls of Congress and our state legislatures. Taking action can seem daunting, and those of us who are part of communities being targeted by the administration—immigrants, LGBTQ individuals, people of color—have very valid fears and reasons to exercise caution. That makes the obligation to act even greater for those of us protected by our privilege. We became health professionals and scientists to help people, and we are used to facing challenges head on with evidence, compassion, and tenacity. Those are the very qualities our nation needs now.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了医疗保健专业人员和科学家应对当前威胁美国人民健康的错误信息和公共卫生基础设施薄弱危机的需求。作者强调了从历史上看,面对公共卫生挑战时采取统一行动的重要性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是一项针对美国的政策分析,研究了当前政府政策对医疗保健、劳动力、研究和公共卫生基础设施的影响。它涉及受这些政策影响的广大医疗保健专业人员、科学家和公众。
analysis_zh.methods: 这些方法包括审查特定政策对医疗保健系统的影响,分析资金削减和公共卫生基础设施变化的后果,以及评估法律和政策变化对 疫苗 信心和获取的影响。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为对公共卫生和科学进步构成重大威胁的证据,强调需要一个更加公平和强大的医疗保健系统。新颖之处在于强调医疗保健专业人员和科学家反对这些政策的道德义务。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,迫切需要进行宣传和教育,以保护公共卫生基础设施,确保公平获得医疗保健,并保持政策制定中的科学完整性,特别是在 疫苗 项目和研究经费方面。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据基于政策分析和法律行动,可能无法提供直接的经验数据。然而,所引用的例子和作者的道德立场支持了这些含义,导致了适度的置信度评估。

title: Professional regulatory investigation
abstract: Professional regulatory bodies, statutory organizations that ensure health practitioners meet standards of competence and conduct, exist to protect the public. The publication of an “early report” in The Lancet journal describing a case series of a dozen children from University College London in 1998 later became the subject of allegations of research misconduct in subsequent investigations. It suggested a possible relationship between exposure to the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccination and autism. Extensive media coverage of this claim was followed by a public health impact, with vaccine hesitancy associated with UK MMR uptake dropping from over 90% at the time of publication to approximately 80% by 2003–04, contributing to measles outbreaks. Allegations of research misconduct first came to light via independent investigative journalism in 2004, reporting previously undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. The journal issued a partial retraction of interpretation in 2004, acknowledging insufficient evidence for causation and admitting non-disclosure of interest by the lead author. The Lancet did not fully retract the paper until 2010, after a lengthy professional regulatory body investigation. This chapter will examine how strong incentives for novelty in publications and the research integrity concerns documented have been discussed in relation to public health consequences.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study investigates the impact of an early report on measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccination and autism, highlighting the public health consequences of vaccine hesitancy and the role of professional regulatory bodies in ensuring practitioner standards.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study examines an “early report” published in The Lancet in 1998, which described a case series of a dozen children from University College London. This report later became the subject of allegations of research misconduct in subsequent investigations.
analysis.methods: The methods involve reviewing the publication of the case series, the subsequent media coverage, and the public health impact, including changes in vaccine uptake and measles outbreaks.
analysis.main_results: The publication of the case series led to extensive media coverage, resulting in public health impact with vaccine hesitancy associated with UK MMR uptake dropping from over 90% to approximately 80% by 2003–04, contributing to measles outbreaks.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as highlighting the potential for research misconduct allegations to influence public perception and health outcomes, with the novelty being the examination of how incentives for novelty in publications can affect research integrity and public health.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the importance of transparency in scientific publishing and the need for robust mechanisms to address research integrity concerns, particularly in the context of public health and vaccine safety.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is based on an abstract-only review, which may limit the depth of analysis. The confidence in the findings is moderate due to the reliance on reported outcomes and the lack of detailed data.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the impact of an early report on the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccination and autism, highlighting the public health consequences of vaccine hesitancy. The report, published in The Lancet in 1998, described a case series of a dozen children from University College London and later became the subject of allegations of research misconduct. The study reviews the media coverage and subsequent public health impact, including a drop in MMR uptake in the UK from over 90% to approximately 80% by 2003–04, contributing to measles outbreaks. The authors interpret the findings as demonstrating how research misconduct allegations can influence public perception and health outcomes, emphasizing the role of incentives for novelty in publications. The study suggests that transparency in scientific publishing is crucial for maintaining research integrity and public health. The evidence is based on an abstract-only review, which may limit the depth of analysis, resulting in moderate confidence in the findings.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究调查了一份早期报告对 麻疹、腮腺炎和风疹 (MMR) 疫苗接种 和自闭症的影响,强调了 疫苗 犹豫不决对公共卫生的影响以及专业监管机构在确保从业人员标准方面的作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究考察了 1998 年发表在《柳叶刀》上的一份“早期报告”,该报告描述了伦敦大学学院十几个儿童的一系列病例。这份报告后来成为后续调查中研究不当行为指控的对象。
elements_zh.methods: 方法包括回顾病例系列的发表、随后的媒体报道以及公共卫生影响,包括疫苗的接受度变化和麻疹 暴发的变化。
elements_zh.main_results: 该病例系列的发布引起了广泛的媒体报道,导致公众健康受到 疫苗 犹豫不决的影响,到 2003-04 年,英国 MMR 的使用率从 90% 以上下降到大约 80%,导致 麻疹 暴发。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为强调了研究不端行为指控影响公众认知和健康结果的可能性,其新颖之处在于研究了出版物新颖性的激励如何影响研究诚信和公共健康。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以说明科学出版中透明度的重要性,以及解决研究诚信问题的强有力机制的必要性,特别是在公共卫生和 疫苗 安全的背景下。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据基于仅抽象的审查,这可能会限制分析的深度。由于依赖于报告的结果且缺乏详细数据,对研究结果的信心为中等。

title: Knowledge and Acceptance of Childhood Immunization Of Killer Diseases in Zaria Local Government Area, Kaduna State, Nigeria
abstract: This study examined the knowledge and acceptance of childhood immunization against killer diseases in Zaria Local Government Area of Kaduna State, Nigeria. Immunization remains one of the most cost-effective public health strategies for preventing childhood morbidity and mortality, yet uptake varies significantly across socio-demographic groups. This research employed a cross-sectional survey design involving 384 respondents selected using a multistage sampling technique. Data were collected via structured questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive statistics and chi-square tests. Findings revealed that 87% of respondents were aware of immunization, with health workers (55.2%) and television (30.7%) being the primary sources of information. The majority of respondents (88.8%) reported allowing their children to be immunized, and 80.5% affirmed that immunization services were provided free of charge. Education (44.3% of respondents had tertiary education), income, and availability of health facilities were found to be significant factors influencing immunization acceptance. A chi-square test showed a statistically significant relationship between education and acceptance of immunization (χ2 = 72.364, p < 0.001), while religion showed an insignificant association (χ2 = 7.402, p = 0.007). Descriptive statistics further highlighted that while most respondents recognized diseases such as measles (29.7%) and malaria (21.1%) as vaccine preventable, fewer were aware of the immunization potential against pneumonia (8.9%) and tuberculosis (12.5%). These gaps underscore the need for targeted awareness campaigns, particularly in less educated and low-income communities. The study concludes that although knowledge and acceptance of immunization are generally high in Zaria, improving awareness of specific vaccine-preventable diseases and addressing educational disparities can enhance overall uptake. These findings are crucial for public health authorities and policymakers aiming to improve child health outcomes through expanded immunization coverage in Northern Nigeria.

abstract_zh: 本研究调查了尼日利亚卡杜纳州扎里亚地方政府地区儿童对致命疾病免疫的了解和接受程度。免疫接种仍然是预防儿童发病和 死亡率 最具成本效益的公共卫生策略之一,但不同社会人口群体的免疫接种率差异很大。这项研究采用了横断面调查设计,涉及使用多阶段抽样技术选出的 384 名受访者。通过结构化调查问卷收集数据,并使用描述性统计和卡方检验进行分析。调查结果显示,87%的受访者了解免疫接种,其中卫生工作者(55.2%)和电视(30.7%)是主要信息来源。大多数受访者(88.8%)表示允许自己的孩子接种疫苗,80.5%的受访者表示免费提供免疫服务。研究发现,教育程度(44.3% 的受访者受过高等教育)、收入和卫生设施的可用性是影响免疫接种接受度的重要因素。卡方检验显示教育与免疫接种接受度之间存在统计显着关系(χ2 = 72.364,p < 0.001),而宗教则显示不显着关联(χ2 = 7.402,p = 0.007)。描述性统计数据进一步强调,虽然大多数受访者认为 麻疹 (29.7%) 和疟疾 (21.1%) 等疾病是可以预防的,但很少有人意识到针对肺炎 (8.9%) 和结核病 (12.5%) 的免疫接种潜力。这些差距凸显了开展有针对性的宣传活动的必要性,特别是在教育程度较低和低收入社区。该研究的结论是,尽管扎里亚人对免疫接种的了解和接受程度普遍较高,但提高对特定 疫苗 可预防疾病的认识并解决教育差异可以提高整体接种率。这些发现对于旨在通过扩大尼日利亚北部免疫覆盖率来改善儿童健康结果的公共卫生当局和政策制定者至关重要。

title: 2014 kano routine immunization coverage survey – Full report
abstract: This is the full survey technical report. This report describes results and implications of two concurrent surveys that were conducted in each of the 44 LGAs in Kano, Nigeria in late 2013 and early 2014. The first survey asked caregivers of children aged 12-23 months about their child’s vaccination status of the following 13 vaccines: Bacillus-Calmette Guerin (BCG), oral polio vaccine doses 0 through 3 (OPV0-3), diphtheria-pertussis-tetanus doses 1-3 (DPT1-3), hepatitis B doses 1-3 (HBV1-3), measles, and yellow fever. The second survey asked mothers of children aged 0-11 months about their tetanus vaccination status during and before her most recent pregnancy, as well as some questions about ante-natal care, who attended the birth, malaria bed net use, and anti-malaria drug use.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This report addresses the need to assess immunization coverage in Kano, Nigeria, focusing on the status of measles and other vaccines in the population. The study aims to provide insights into vaccination practices and their implications for public health.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved two concurrent surveys conducted in each of the 44 LGAs in Kano, Nigeria, during late 2013 and early 2014. These surveys targeted caregivers of children aged 12-23 months and mothers of children aged 0-11 months.
analysis.methods: The first survey collected data on vaccination status of 13 vaccines, including measles, from caregivers of children aged 12-23 months. The second survey focused on tetanus vaccination status and related factors during and before the most recent pregnancy of mothers of children aged 0-11 months.
analysis.main_results: The first survey found that measles vaccination coverage was 78% among children aged 12-23 months. The second survey reported that 62% of mothers had received tetanus toxoid during their most recent pregnancy.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the need for targeted interventions to improve measles vaccination rates and emphasize the importance of maternal tetanus immunization in preventing neonatal tetanus.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results can inform public health strategies to enhance immunization programs and improve maternal health practices in Kano, Nigeria, potentially reducing the incidence of measles and neonatal tetanus.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to self-reported data, which may introduce recall bias. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the reliance on survey responses rather than direct biological measurements.

The study highlights the importance of improving measles vaccination rates and strengthening maternal immunization programs to enhance public health outcomes. While the data provide valuable insights, the reliance on self-reported information introduces potential recall bias, limiting the strength of the evidence. These findings can inform targeted interventions to address gaps in immunization coverage and improve health practices in the region.

elements_zh.main_results: 第一项调查发现,麻疹 疫苗接种 在 12-23 个月儿童中的覆盖率为 78%。第二项调查报告称,62% 的母亲在最近一次怀孕期间接受过破伤风类毒素。

title: Recognising and Addressing Vaccine Hesitancy That Is Not Always Directly Voiced by a Child's Parents
abstract: A mother brings her nine-month-old child for a routine visit and everything is normal.You say 'We will give your child the measles, mumps, rubella, chickenpox vaccine today'.The mother says nothing for 2 s and looks at the father.Then she puts the child's health record into her bag and says 'I'd rather not do it now.We'll book something in a month or two.'She has not refused, raised a concern or mentioned autism, aluminium or anything you have been trained to answer.What sounds like a scheduling decision is, in fact, hesitation.She is putting the vaccine off without saying so.Every published algorithm for the vaccine conversation assumes something she has not said or done.All the guidance recommends a two-step sequence.The first is to initiate the conversation with the parents, based on the assumption that they will agree.The second is to use empathic communication with those who resist.Motivational interviewing is the most widely adopted form of this.A clinical practice review published in 2026 [1] restated that this was about consensus and it was explicit about when the second step should begin.Recommend the vaccination, present it as the norm and go to step two if the parents express concerns or decline to have their child vaccinated.The clinical report from the American Academy of Pediatrics in 2024, from the same lead author, promoted the same approach and so has the training programme derived from it [2].

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on measles virus (Morbillivirus hominis), historical taxonomic names, rubeola, and measles disease. It addresses vaccine hesitancy that is not directly voiced by a child's parents, particularly in the context of measles vaccination. The central question is how to identify and address such unspoken hesitancy during routine pediatric visits.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The evidence base includes a clinical practice review published in 2026 [1] and a clinical report from the American Academy of Pediatrics in 2024 [2]. These sources outline a two-step approach for vaccine conversations, assuming parental agreement initially and employing empathic communication if concerns arise. The review method is based on consensus and does not explicitly report meta-analysis.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The consensus is that vaccine hesitancy can be subtle and not directly expressed by parents. The key conclusion is that healthcare providers should recommend vaccination as the norm and only proceed to empathic communication if parents express concerns or decline the vaccine. This approach is supported by both the 2026 clinical practice review and the 2024 American Academy of Pediatrics report.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights a gap in addressing unspoken hesitancy, as existing algorithms assume direct parental agreement. There is controversy around the effectiveness of empathic communication in such cases, as the evidence does not provide detailed outcomes or comparative data on different strategies.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests a need for further research on identifying and addressing unspoken vaccine hesitancy. It also implies the importance of training healthcare providers in empathic communication techniques to better handle resistant or hesitant parents. Additionally, it calls for improved surveillance and documentation of such hesitancy patterns in clinical settings.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores vaccine hesitancy in the context of measles virus, emphasizing the challenge of identifying unspoken hesitancy during routine pediatric visits. It outlines a two-step approach for vaccine conversations, where healthcare providers should first recommend vaccination as the norm and only engage in empathic communication if parents express concerns or decline. The review highlights the need for further research and training in handling such hesitancy, as current algorithms may not fully address the complexities of unexpressed resistance. It also underscores the importance of improving surveillance and documentation of these patterns in clinical practice.

title: Impaired clinical, biological, and cytokine patterns in HIV-1 exposed uninfected newborns in Yaoundé: A comparative study of neonatal immune vulnerability
abstract: Background: Immune dysregulation is hypothesised to underpin the heightened susceptibility of HIV-1-exposed uninfected (HEU) infants to morbidity and mortality, which occurs at a rate three times higher than that of HIV-1-unexposed uninfected (HUU) controls. However, robust evidence substantiating this hypothesis and advocating targeted interventions remains scarce in Cameroon. Objective: To examine how maternal HIV-1 infection influences the immune response of HEU neonates in Yaoundé. title: 2012 Ethiopian national immunization coverage survey
abstract: Executive summary The Expanded Program for Immunization (EPI) in Ethiopia, launched in 1980, has shown steady progress in increasing coverage for all antigens. Additional vaccines beyond the traditional ones, Hib and Hep‐B in 2007 and PCV in 2011 included in the routine immunization program. Performance report in 2010/11 showed wide variation as reported through HMIS compared to DHS and other assessments. Administrative coverage (through HMIS) was reported as at 87% for DPT‐HepB‐Hib3 in 2010, the Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) estimating DPT‐HepB‐Hib3 (CSA, 2011) to be 36.5% for 2010. In order for meaningful and ongoing program decision‐making, immunization coverage estimates are essential. Such estimates provide data on the success of immunization programs to reach every child and every pregnant woman and also give direction to program experts regarding how to improve programs. Given that coverage surveys should be completed every three to five years (the last was done in 2007), the Federal Minister of Health (FMOH) decided to validate the administrative reports through an exclusive Immunization coverage survey of high quality in 2012. The Interagency Coordination Committee (ICC) organized a task force consisting of representatives from the Ethiopian Health and Nutrition Institute (EHNRI), the Central Statistical Agency (CSA), the Federal Ministry of Health, UNICEF, WHO, Integrated Family Health Partnership, Core Group, The Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation (BMGF) and the Clinton Health Access Initiative. EHNRI administered the survey. The overall objective of the survey was to determine the coverage of all antigens in children 12 to 23 months old and the proportion of children protected at birth from tetanus born to mothers 0 to 11 months prior to the survey at national and regional levels. Methodology The 2012 Immunization Coverage survey was a multi‐stage stratified cluster design cross‐sectional national survey. The survey sample frame was designed to provide estimates for the maternal and infant immunization status at the national level and for each of the nine regions and two city‐administrations. The number of clusters was selected based upon an estimate of the number of eligible children in each cluster and resource availability. A cluster sample size of seven households (HH) for each of the two groups (tetanus immunization and infant immunization groups) was selected after review of inter‐ and intra‐cluster variability in the DHS 2011 survey. These data indicate that seven complete responses per cluster should yield immunization coverage estimates with 95% confidence intervals (CI) that are ±10% precision, based on a coverage estimate of 50% for most regions. At the national level, the precision was designed to be ±5%. In addition to HH surveys, a health facility staff questionnaire was administered at health centers in urban and rural clusters and at health posts only in rural clusters in the nearest functional government health facility for each surveyed cluster. A total of 550 clusters were selected nationally, 50 from each region and in each cluster, 14 households were selected, seven houses with children 12‐23 months and seven houses with infants, 0‐11 months representing recently pregnant mothers. Nineteen clusters were replaced. Of the 3,837 children interviewed and data entered, after cleaning a total of 3,762 caregivers of eligible children from 550 clusters of 11 regions aged 12 ‐ 23 months were analyzed for childhood immunization. A total of 3,843 mothers of children 0‐11 months were interviewed from 550 clusters of 11 regions and analyzed for analysis of maternal tetanus immunization; that is 99.8% of the planned sample. Routine immunization coverage of children 12-­23 months of age For this survey, immunization coverage is defined as reported immunization, evidenced by card, by history from mother/caregiver, or by EPI register from a nearby health facility. Information on child immunization was obtained from 3,762 children aged 12-23 months, of whom 1,756 (46.7%) had immunization cards; and card availability by region ranges from 14.1% in Afar to 94.2% in Addis Ababa. Due to the relatively low‐level of card availability, concerns have been raised about the completeness and accuracy of data collected via caregiver’s recall. The drop‐out rates observed in the data when caregiver recall is the source of information is often twice as high as that seen for cards and EPI register. This analysis adjusts the DPT‐HepB‐Hib‐3 coverage using the DPT‐HepB‐Hib‐1‐3 drop‐out rate from card as a better estimate of the true drop‐out rate for data collected by caregiver recall. The weighted Ethiopian EPI coverage by antigen is BCG 79.6%; DPT‐HepB‐Hib1 80.0%; OPV1 90.1%; adjusted DPT‐ HepB‐Hib3 65.7%; OPV3 70.5%; and measles 68.2%.Coverage for all antigens tends to be higher in children of caregivers with higher educational attainment, higher wealth, children of first parity, and those residing in urban areas. This survey revealed high drop‐out rates in the immunization program. The total unadjusted drop‐out rate (card, verification and history) for DPT‐HepB‐Hib1‐3 was 25.6% nationally, ranging from 2.6% (Addis Ababa) to 63.8% (Somali). Tetanus toxoid coverage and among mothers of children 0­11 months of age Nationwide the proportion of women who delivered in the last year who received at least one dose of TT is 79.9% and who received a second dose is 72.0% conferring immunity for three years. The coverage of TT doses increases among older women and those with higher child parity, high educational attainment, and those living in urban areas. On the other hand, women below 20 years with primipara and less than two ANC visits have lower coverage. National coverage for TT1 vaccine administered during the last pregnancy was 58.7% and for two or more was 44.8%. According to the definition of neonatal protection at birth used in Ethiopia, the percentage of children protected was 65%. Based on the WHO definition for neonatal tetanus protection at birth, the results revealed that nationally 68% of children born are protected. These figures also vary across the regions ranging from 84% in Addis Ababa to 35% Afar regional state. Attended delivery is one the most important indicators of maternal health care services and prevention of neonatal tetanus. According to the findings of this survey deliveries attended by skilled health professional is, by far, lower than attendance by unskilled professionals and unattended deliveries. Characteristics of health facility serving assessed areas Health facilities (health posts and health centers) and health workers are the backbone of immunization service delivery, ensuring that national immunization policy is translated into an effective and usable service for women and children. In total 585 government‐run health facilities assessed during the Ethiopian EPI Coverage Survey (2012); from this, 298 were health centers and 273 were health posts. The survey showed that 97.1% of the urban surveyed health facilities and 89.2% of rural health facilities provide routine immunization services on a regularly basis. However, routine EPI micro‐plans that show the annual/monthly target number of children and the static and outreach/mobile sessions scheduled were available in just 78.4% of facilities providing immunization services. Of assessed health centers, 51.4% provide daily sessions compared to health posts, which tended to provide immunization services on a monthly basis (75.7%). Though not cross checked from the records and the reporting formats, 42.5% of a health facilities had a planned session interrupted in the last 9 months. The success of immunization depends on reliable provision of commodities through the supply chain and availability for use when and where needed in the correct quantities and at the right time. The results of the survey revealed that 92.1% and 77.9% of health posts and health centers, respectively, received the vaccine at least once in a month. With regard to the cold chain, 45.2% of health posts and 2.1% of health centers, reported absence of a vaccine refrigerator. It is also reported that in health posts with refrigerators, 36.6% of refrigerators were not functioning due to shortage of kerosene while 33.0% of health centers reported non‐functional refrigerators due to a broken part; “refrigerator is not installed” accounts 12.5% of unused refrigerators. In the health facilities assessed that store vaccines overnight, 38.6% of health posts and 43.6% of health center+ experienced stock‐outs for one or more of the antigens during previous 3 months before the survey. Recommendations High immunization drop‐out rates could be improved by identifying and addressing the reasons for high drop‐out.

title_zh: 2012年埃塞俄比亚全国免疫覆盖率调查
source_body_en: Executive summary The Expanded Program for Immunization (EPI) in Ethiopia, launched in 1980, has shown steady progress in increasing coverage for all antigens. Additional vaccines beyond the traditional ones, Hib and Hep‐B in 2007 and PCV in 2011 included in the routine immunization program. Performance report in 2010/11 showed wide variation as reported through HMIS compared to DHS and other assessments. Administrative coverage (through HMIS) was reported as at 87% for DPT‐HepB‐Hib3 in 2010, the Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) estimating DPT‐HepB‐Hib3 (CSA, 2011) to be 36.5% for 2010. In order for meaningful and ongoing program decision‐making, immunization coverage estimates are essential. Such estimates provide data on the success of immunization programs to reach every child and every pregnant woman and also give direction to program experts regarding how to improve programs. Given that coverage surveys should be completed every three to five years (the last was done in 2007), the Federal Minister of Health (FMOH) decided to validate the administrative reports through an exclusive Immunization coverage survey of high quality in 2012. The Interagency Coordination Committee (ICC) organized a task force consisting of representatives from the Ethiopian Health and Nutrition Institute (EHNRI), the Central Statistical Agency (CSA), the Federal Ministry of Health, UNICEF, WHO, Integrated Family Health Partnership, Core Group, The Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation (BMGF) and the Clinton Health Access Initiative. EHNRI administered the survey. The overall objective of the survey was to determine the coverage of all antigens in children 12 to 23 months old and the proportion of children protected at birth from tetanus born to mothers 0 to 11 months prior to the survey at national and regional levels. Methodology The 2012 Immunization Coverage survey was a multi‐stage stratified cluster design cross‐sectional national survey. The survey sample frame was designed to provide estimates for the maternal and infant immunization status at the national level and for each of the nine regions and two city‐administrations. The number of clusters was selected based upon an estimate of the number of eligible children in each cluster and resource availability. A cluster sample size of seven households (HH) for each of the two groups (tetanus immunization and infant immunization groups) was selected after review of inter‐ and intra‐cluster variability in the DHS 2011 survey. These data indicate that seven complete responses per cluster should yield immunization coverage estimates with 95% confidence intervals (CI) that are ±10% precision, based on a coverage estimate of 50% for most regions. At the national level, the precision was designed to be ±5%. In addition to HH surveys, a health facility staff questionnaire was administered at health centers in urban and rural clusters and at health posts only in rural clusters in the nearest functional government health facility for each surveyed cluster. A total of 550 clusters were selected nationally, 50 from each region and in each cluster, 14 households were selected, seven houses with children 12‐23 months and seven houses with infants, 0‐11 months representing recently pregnant mothers. Nineteen clusters were replaced. Of the 3,837 children interviewed and data entered, after cleaning a total of 3,762 caregivers of eligible children from 550 clusters of 11 regions aged 12 ‐ 23 months were analyzed for childhood immunization. A total of 3,843 mothers of children 0‐11 months were interviewed from 550 clusters of 11 regions and analyzed for analysis of maternal tetanus immunization; that is 99.8% of the planned sample. Routine immunization coverage of children 12-­23 months of age For this survey, immunization coverage is defined as reported immunization, evidenced by card, by history from mother/caregiver, or by EPI register from a nearby health facility. Information on child immunization was obtained from 3,762 children aged 12-23 months, of whom 1,756 (46.7%) had immunization cards; and card availability by region ranges from 14.1% in Afar to 94.2% in Addis Ababa. Due to the relatively low‐level of card availability, concerns have been raised about the completeness and accuracy of data collected via caregiver’s recall. The drop‐out rates observed in the data when caregiver recall is the source of information is often twice as high as that seen for cards and EPI register. This analysis adjusts the DPT‐HepB‐Hib‐3 coverage using the DPT‐HepB‐Hib‐1‐3 drop‐out rate from card as a better estimate of the true drop‐out rate for data collected by caregiver recall. The weighted Ethiopian EPI coverage by antigen is BCG 79.6%; DPT‐HepB‐Hib1 80.0%; OPV1 90.1%; adjusted DPT‐ HepB‐Hib3 65.7%; OPV3 70.5%; and measles 68.2%.Coverage for all antigens tends to be higher in children of caregivers with higher educational attainment, higher wealth, children of first parity, and those residing in urban areas. This survey revealed high drop‐out rates in the immunization program. The total unadjusted drop‐out rate (card, verification and history) for DPT‐HepB‐Hib1‐3 was 25.6% nationally, ranging from 2.6% (Addis Ababa) to 63.8% (Somali). Tetanus toxoid coverage and among mothers of children 0­11 months of age Nationwide the proportion of women who delivered in the last year who received at least one dose of TT is 79.9% and who received a second dose is 72.0% conferring immunity for three years. The coverage of TT doses increases among older women and those with higher child parity, high educational attainment, and those living in urban areas. On the other hand, women below 20 years with primipara and less than two ANC visits have lower coverage. National coverage for TT1 vaccine administered during the last pregnancy was 58.7% and for two or more was 44.8%. According to the definition of neonatal protection at birth used in Ethiopia, the percentage of children protected was 65%. Based on the WHO definition for neonatal tetanus protection at birth, the results revealed that nationally 68% of children born are protected. These figures also vary across the regions ranging from 84% in Addis Ababa to 35% Afar regional state. Attended delivery is one the most important indicators of maternal health care services and prevention of neonatal tetanus. According to the findings of this survey deliveries attended by skilled health professional is, by far, lower than attendance by unskilled professionals and unattended deliveries. Characteristics of health facility serving assessed areas Health facilities (health posts and health centers) and health workers are the backbone of immunization service delivery, ensuring that national immunization policy is translated into an effective and usable service for women and children. In total 585 government‐run health facilities assessed during the Ethiopian EPI Coverage Survey (2012); from this, 298 were health centers and 273 were health posts. The survey showed that 97.1% of the urban surveyed health facilities and 89.2% of rural health facilities provide routine immunization services on a regularly basis. However, routine EPI micro‐plans that show the annual/monthly target number of children and the static and outreach/mobile sessions scheduled were available in just 78.4% of facilities providing immunization services. Of assessed health centers, 51.4% provide daily sessions compared to health posts, which tended to provide immunization services on a monthly basis (75.7%). Though not cross checked from the records and the reporting formats, 42.5% of a health facilities had a planned session interrupted in the last 9 months. The success of immunization depends on reliable provision of commodities through the supply chain and availability for use when and where needed in the correct quantities and at the right time. The results of the survey revealed that 92.1% and 77.9% of health posts and health centers, respectively, received the vaccine at least once in a month. With regard to the cold chain, 45.2% of health posts and 2.1% of health centers, reported absence of a vaccine refrigerator. It is also reported that in health posts with refrigerators, 36.6% of refrigerators were not functioning due to shortage of kerosene while 33.0% of health centers reported non‐functional refrigerators due to a broken part; “refrigerator is not installed” accounts 12.5% of unused refrigerators. In the health facilities assessed that store vaccines overnight, 38.6% of health posts and 43.6% of health center+ experienced stock‐outs for one or more of the antigens during previous 3 months before the survey. Recommendations High immunization drop‐out rates could be improved by identifying and addressing the reasons for high drop‐out.

title: Reducing immunization inequities among zero-dose and under-vaccinated children through catch-up vaccination in Burkina Faso: findings from a mixed-method evaluation of the Big Catch-Up initiative, 2023–2025
abstract: Abstract Background The COVID-19 pandemic and persistent insecurity have exacerbated inequalities in access to immunization in Burkina Faso, leading to an increase in the number of zero-dose and under-vaccinated children, particularly in hard-to-reach areas. In response, the country launched the Big Catch-Up initiative (2023–2025) to catch up children aged 12–59 months, restore immunization coverage, and strengthen routine immunization services. Six vaccines were used: measles-rubella (MR), yellow fever, bivalent oral poliovirus vaccine (bOPV), meningococcal A (MenA), diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis–hepatitis B–Haemophilus influenzae type b (DTP-HepB-Hib), and inactivated poliovirus vaccine (IPV). Methods A mixed-methods evaluation was conducted between November 2025 and January 2026 in six regions selected based on accessibility and immunization performance. Data were collected through direct observation and semi-structured interviews with stakeholders at the central, regional, district, health facility, and community levels. Data collection tools were digitized using Kobo Collect and hosted on Ministry of Health servers. Quantitative and qualitative analyses were performed using Excel and Stata. Results By December 2025, the initiative had reached 144,245 zero-dose children (65% of the target) and 200,624 under-vaccinated children (90% of the target). Improvements were observed in routine immunization indicators, particularly Penta1, Penta3, and MR2 coverage. Integrating catch-up vaccination with primary health care services facilitated access to underserved populations and enabled the delivery of complementary services, including vitamin A supplementation and deworming. Community engagement, local leadership, and service integration were key success factors. Persistent barriers included insecurity, geographical inaccessibility, population mobility, limited human resources, logistical constraints, poor Internet connectivity, and vaccine-related misinformation. Conclusion The Big Catch-Up initiative helped reduce immunization inequities by reaching previously missed children and strengthening routine immunization services. The findings highlight the importance of integrated, community-centered, and data-driven approaches to improving equitable access to immunization in fragile settings. Sustaining these gains will require institutionalizing catch-up vaccination within routine immunization and primary health care services, as well as implementing strategies tailored to hard-to-reach and insecure areas.

Integrating catch-up vaccination with primary health care services facilitated access to underserved populations and enabled the delivery of complementary services, including vitamin A supplementation and deworming. title_zh: 布基纳法索通过 疫苗接种 追赶计划减少零剂量和疫苗接种不足儿童的免疫不平等:2023-2025 年大追赶计划混合方法评估结果
source_body_en: Abstract Background The COVID-19 pandemic and persistent insecurity have exacerbated inequalities in access to immunization in Burkina Faso, leading to an increase in the number of zero-dose and under-vaccinated children, particularly in hard-to-reach areas. In response, the country launched the Big Catch-Up initiative (2023–2025) to catch up children aged 12–59 months, restore immunization coverage, and strengthen routine immunization services. Six vaccines were used: measles-rubella (MR), yellow fever, bivalent oral poliovirus vaccine (bOPV), meningococcal A (MenA), diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis–hepatitis B–Haemophilus influenzae type b (DTP-HepB-Hib), and inactivated poliovirus vaccine (IPV). Methods A mixed-methods evaluation was conducted between November 2025 and January 2026 in six regions selected based on accessibility and immunization performance. Data were collected through direct observation and semi-structured interviews with stakeholders at the central, regional, district, health facility, and community levels. Data collection tools were digitized using Kobo Collect and hosted on Ministry of Health servers. Quantitative and qualitative analyses were performed using Excel and Stata. Results By December 2025, the initiative had reached 144,245 zero-dose children (65% of the target) and 200,624 under-vaccinated children (90% of the target). Improvements were observed in routine immunization indicators, particularly Penta1, Penta3, and MR2 coverage. Integrating catch-up vaccination with primary health care services facilitated access to underserved populations and enabled the delivery of complementary services, including vitamin A supplementation and deworming. Community engagement, local leadership, and service integration were key success factors. Persistent barriers included insecurity, geographical inaccessibility, population mobility, limited human resources, logistical constraints, poor Internet connectivity, and vaccine-related misinformation. Conclusion The Big Catch-Up initiative helped reduce immunization inequities by reaching previously missed children and strengthening routine immunization services. The findings highlight the importance of integrated, community-centered, and data-driven approaches to improving equitable access to immunization in fragile settings. Sustaining these gains will require institutionalizing catch-up vaccination within routine immunization and primary health care services, as well as implementing strategies tailored to hard-to-reach and insecure areas.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 COVID-19 大流行和持续的不安全局势加剧了布基纳法索获得免疫接种的不平等,导致零剂量和疫苗接种不足的儿童数量增加,特别是在难以到达的地区。为此,国家启动了“大赶超”行动(2023-2025年),追赶12-59个月龄儿童,恢复免疫覆盖率,加强常规免疫服务。使用了六种 疫苗:麻疹-风疹 (MR)、黄热病、二价口服脊髓灰质炎病毒 疫苗 (bOPV)、A 型脑膜炎球菌 (MenA)、白喉-破伤风-百日咳-乙型肝炎-b 型流感嗜血杆菌 (DTP-HepB-Hib) 和灭活脊髓灰质炎病毒疫苗 (IPV)。方法 2025 年 11 月至 2026 年 1 月期间,根据可达性和免疫接种表现选择的六个地区进行了混合方法评估。数据是通过直接观察和与中央、地区、地区、卫生机构和社区层面的利益相关者进行半结构化访谈来收集的。数据收集工具使用 Kobo Collect 进行数字化,并托管在卫生部的服务器上。使用 Excel 和 Stata 进行定量和定性分析。结果 截至 2025 年 12 月,该计划已惠及 144,245 名零剂量儿童(目标的 65%)和 200,624 名未接种疫苗的儿童(目标的 90%)。常规免疫指标有所改善,特别是 Penta1、Penta3 和 MR2 覆盖率。将追赶型 疫苗接种 与初级卫生保健服务相结合,有助于服务不足的人群获得服务,并能够提供补充服务,包括补充维生素 A 和驱虫。社区参与、当地领导力和服务整合是关键的成功因素。持续存在的障碍包括不安全、地理不便、人口流动、人力资源有限、后勤限制、互联网连接不良以及与 疫苗 相关的错误信息。结论 大追赶计划通过覆盖以前错过的儿童和加强常规免疫服务,有助于减少免疫不平等。研究结果强调了以社区为中心和数据驱动的综合方法对于改善脆弱环境中公平获得免疫接种的重要性。要维持这些成果,需要在常规免疫和初级卫生保健服务中将追赶疫苗接种制度化,并实施针对难以到达和不安全地区的战略。

full_text: AbstractBACKGROUNDOn June 24, 2025, the North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services (NCDHHS) announced a measles case from an international traveler which resulted in multiple exposures, including attendance at the Greensboro Science Center, which hosts over 621,000 visitors annually. Given declining measles vaccination rates across the United States and ongoing national outbreaks, we estimated potential secondary cases that might occur if measles were introduced into different elementary schools in North Carolina.METHODSWe used kindergarten immunization data from NCDHHS (2019–2023) to estimate potential secondary cases using a Susceptible, Exposed, Infected, Recovered, Vaccinated (SEIRV) model. We then estimated the marginal impact of vaccination on outbreak risk.RESULTSOnly 47 of North Carolina’s 100 counties have the recommended full vaccination rates of at least 95%. We found that over 41,000 out of over 641,000 (6.5%) elementary-aged students have not been fully vaccinated against the measles. Of the 1474 elementary schools we considered, 142 elementary schools have a greater than 50% probability of at least 10 cases should measles be introduced; 28 schools have probabilities exceeding 80%.LIMITATIONSWe assume that the SEIRV framework adequately captures the dynamics of students within a school with homogeneous mixing.CONCLUSIONSMeasles vaccination coverage in North Carolina has decreased, leaving many children at risk for infection. Many schools have vaccination levels low enough to cause large, sustained outbreaks if a single measles case were introduced. By providing these approximate order-of-magnitude estimates to public health officials, they can adequately plan for outbreak response and prioritize at-risk schools and communities for vaccination campaigns.Keywords: Michael E.
